After losing our base, all vehicles, everything gathered since release, and only a couple weeks notice for transfers, I will never return to this game again... What a waste. 
All the other problems are another story, and I wont get into it as there's 100s of other reviews complaining about these issues. However, how poorly they did the world transfers is the end of the road for me. Never again will I touch a Funcom game.

It was great at the start. Very immersive universe. But unfortunately after awhile, the game mechanics started getting repetitive - farm, kill, extract water, craft stuff...and once you hit the endgame as a solo player without a guild, the game gets pretty stale. Would have loved to have loved it, but unfortunately without a decent endgame mechanic, it starts to become a chore.

Don't buy, as the main quest line is bugged for a lot of players. The small stuff first: The game starts off really cool and quite motivating. You can really immerse yourself in the Dune universe. After a while the game turns into a lot of grinding to quite literally keep the lights on in your base. Also, there is a lot of quest design that is just flat-out bad. The flow within the quests, but also the flow from quest to quest is not as immersive as you would hope from a game in this otherwise really cool setting. 

HOWEVER, what really killed the game for me, is that the main quest is bugged and I cannot continue with it. This is a bug that the publisher/developers knew about since at least Summer 2025 and I haven't seen anybody that reported the bug, who received any solution. My bug reports and requests for help that were sent to the publisher/developer led to nothing and I am now either starting over after 151 hours in the hope that the questline is not bugged this time, or I could just play something with a better game design. I think I will do the latter. This is an unacceptable state for a fully launched game.

Game started strong but end game is a huge disappointment...unless you like groups of griefers rolling around ganking you while you try to get end game MK6 upgrades. End game is only for griefing PvP a$$hats. 6+ griefers stormed my base and killed me and looted all of my base located in the Deep Desert. The main problem was that I actually was able to make it back to my base, where they just all gathered outside and waited for a sandstorm (that temporarily takes your shields down ) and they can enter your base, destroy your sub-fife, and then kill you and loot and dismantle all of your base.

Stupid design. If I make it to my base, no one should be able to enter or destroy. I quit... you can have this BS....

The ONLY way to see end game is to be in a large group or guild that can PvP to obtain the last tier upgrades. If you are a solo player, you will NEVER see end game gear, period.... unless you just rent your own private server..... but even then, its a rinse and repeat play from the time you start.

All the wrecks and stations are identical from start to finish, just a copy and paste around the world.

Was fun until you realize, once you get to Duraluminum, you have seen all the content there is to see....everything else is just a rinse and repeat with no real goal, just to farm.....

Super enjoyable survival game, once you figure out the sun and water game really gets enjoyable. Challenging NPCs. Flexible PVE / PVP rules. Wonderful visuals. Sometimes you eat the worm and sometime the worm eats you. Ok the worm always eats you, but that is why you are here.

Anything positive regarding this game is greatly overshadowed by the fact that all of your efforts could easily end up being for nothing not due to gameplay or any fault of your own but rather from being booted from the server for unscheduled maintenance coupled with not even the slightest in customer support.
It's a great game But I WANT MY PVP BACK. But this game is not for the 60$ the game it like a 30$ game.

Fun gameplay loop, amazing lore building, good base building. Really fun to immerse yourself in the Dune universe with this game. The Chapter 3 update shows that the devs care about making the game better. Hopefully the community gets a little bigger again and the game will be developed and supported for a long time.

Starting area in game and the base building and vehicles are awesome however the end game really is a let down, and even worse is the mix of PvPers and PvEers, its being a constant problem from the beginning and still not resolved, why they didn't just have PvP and PvE seperate servers ?

Pretty soon there will be no more players to complain and Funcom will be out of business. Their only chance is to correct course ASAP and fix what their paying customers want, stop forcing endgame pvp and create endgame pve like WoW or FF14 or The Matrix Online or something had that engages players who want to be solo or like pve and just want to explore the world.

I played the game for the first week then got bored and never came back because of all the problems this game had, and I am one of the biggest Dune fans out there, my aunt had the original Dune novels and handed them down to me over 30 years ago. This world had so much potential, it looked fantastic.. but rollbacks and progression losses and pvp being shoved down our throats with nothing fun to do at the end of the game completely ruined things.

One day this game will close and we will all look back on what could have been if bad leadership had not controlled everything.

My girlfriend and I have over 140 hours in the game. One time we didn’t log in and forgot to refill the power generators. When we finally came back, our entire base was completely wiped — all resources gone, all money gone, and every single device dismantled into parts.

This issue has been reported countless times by players on Steam, YouTube, and Reddit, but the devs haven’t addressed it. They even admitted it’s a bug and said they’ll add an update so NPCs can’t destroy the sublim that manages the base (since other players can’t destroy it directly). The problem is, players are now baiting NPCs to attack your sublim, letting them destroy it, then placing their own sublim and draining all your resources to zero — leaving nothing but trash behind.

This game doesn't respect your time, it is not a single player game at all and your required to keep your generators powered on even if it's been 3 month and your bored. The new content is the same as the old content. This game feels like playing an EA sports game. The lowest level of care and attention.
Saddest game to see die. You fly around and you can literally see bases decay and the server slowly die.

I have been a long-time Conan Exiles player and while I knew FUNCOM was good at creating atmosphere, I had strong doubts about them pulling this off technologically. But I gave them the benefit od the doubt and they really pulled it off. The world is amazing, things work reasonably well (with some issues, but that was to be expected) and the gameplay is great. In the head start, I felt panic as Sandworms chased me down, elation when I took of in my Ornithopter for the first day, pride in the base we managed to build, and amazed by the epicness of it all. 

I am sure I will spend thousands of hours in this game.

Dune: Awakening combines an amazing story line with spectacular gameplay. Hours of enjoyment without getting stale, and new content coming makes it that much more thrilling. I have been gaming for 40 years and this is hands down one of the best I've ever played.

Game has vastly improved since launch.

Yet, devs just let a game breaking, currency duping exploit fester for a while, resulting in billions upon billions of Solari being injected into the economy and they have done nothing but a quick fix to patch it. Instead of proper explanation, we are thrown a "x2 loot/xp" event. This follows several material dupes, where most of the mats also stayed in the economy.

Baffling. Devs truly think all they need to do is throw a few bones and people will stay. In the current state of devs not giving a rat's arse about the game's integrity, you really shouldn't buy this product unless they, one day, decide to release fresh start servers with no character migration possible.

A close replica of the Spice world from the Dune book series. The survival and challenges are realistic and fair, but the game can be set to a harder difficulty level. Make sure you have a good graphics card and CPU.

I don't mind dying due to my own stupidity. But losing hours or work and grinding for a bug or glitch, that I can't abide. There's no learning curve for that. And after losing my thopter and everything I was carrying today through no fault of my own, I'm done. And from what I hear the end game isn't much anyway.

I am a very casual gamer, so bases falling apart without repairs overtime really set me back if I decided to step away for a week or so for vacation / other priorities. For me, this ruined my experience just progressing through the story portion prior to the end game. I would login and find half my bass in ruins with storage containers destroyed.

The gameplay itself, if you are a bit more active of a gamer, is seemingly fun. Gather materials, build stuff, kill stuff, risk it all in the open sands. The different classes, vehicle customizations, weapons...all were pretty fun so far.

The story so far was meh imo but then again I only did some of the main storyline and just side quests before throwing in the towel.

Never got to the end game.

If you are not a casual player OR have a group of friends to play with to regularly take turns with base upkeep...this may be a game worth exploring. But for me, it is a no...which is unfortunate cuz I love Dune.
Game, when it works, is fun and arguably was worth the price of admission. The game crashing for the 100th time is not fun.

This game is not at all what I thought. I am a huge fan of the Dune series, and I can say this game has no soul. I thought the survival part was only a side show, something to do IF you really want to. I wanted to do big things on Arrakis, not scrape through f-ing garbage. What in the hell were you thinking Funcom?! Why isn't there a game play option that doesn't involve endlessly crushing rocks and melting metal scraps? And what is the story? Find the Fremen. Ok, then what? What happens when I find them? Do I lead them in the Jihad, to I become Duke? No, I just go on to scrape some more garbage... Very very disappointing...

I kind of wish you could give ratings on this platform because honestly the game isn't ALL bad. If I were to rate it before you hit Plasteel level crafting, I'd say this is one of the better games I've ever played. However, once you hit that threshold, the entire game changes.

If you want to build anything, it's a terrific grind, like 10-100 times the amount of grinding needed to build anything at Plasteel level. Then spice farming, which is needed to make just about everything, can only be done in small patches unless you want to go up against the PVP mafia.

The game WANTS you to PVP and get griefed, it seems like. Even in the PVE zones, some quests force you to enter PVP areas (why are crashed ships PVP areas anyway?).

And while I appreciate that your bases can't last forever, keeping things powered is a constant chore.

If I had to boil it all down, it's just this. Up until Plasteel, it was a fun game. Now it's no longer a game, it's my second job.

so close to being a great game, just need the small bugs that litter the game to be cleaned up. after that it needs to expand on the dune lore and worlds, creating more gameplay for the players. more story and side missions and not just new locations on arrakis, but new worlds.
game had potential and was killed when the first monthly update only added early game tools

Super fun game. Completely unfinished story and late game. Everything is great uh....right up until you get to deep desert.

Deep desert makes you ask yourself a lot of things.
-Why is everything late game locked to this single place?
-How did someone just steal my vehicle miles away from any solid land while wearing nothing but underwear?
-Why did a server connection issue just eat my late game ornithopter?
-How are all these people firing unlimited missiles, flying at the speed of lightning and never needing any water?
-Why did my camera just get pulled across the map to watch someone dance before crashing to desk top?
All this and more can easily be chalked up to the mysteries of Arrakis, but more than likely will make you question your purchase in the first place. Which is what you should do. Highly recommend letting this bad boy cook for another year of development or more before spending any money on it. Paying full price for an early access game that is more unfinished than an indie title with a single dev, coming from Funcom is ridiculous.

(There will be custom servers for Ark, Conan Exiles, Garry's mod, Fallout 4 that are dune themed before they manage to fix any of this.)

Edit, I still play rarely hoping this will change- just saying, give it a lil while to cook lmao. It's fun, but definitely not a finished product.

Game also exceeded my expectations. One last thing, the Ornithopters are worth it. So much fun to fly.

the first 70 hours of story really good.

DD and end game are garbage and almost ruin the rest of the experience.

Loot scaling isnt viable and the only end game strat is rockets from thopters in a group. absolute trash.

Draw distance is also trash so you cant see people in time to runaway.

all over if you like dune and want a fun dune game with friends first 70 hours is awesome. rest of game will have you pulling your hair out.

The game is fine unless you play the multiplayer. Sure it does look scenery until you get to the gameplay part which you have to grind a lot of resources to build up your character/base. Unless you are on singleplayer or play on a custom multiplayer server with less required resources, I doubt I had a good time going back and forth just to grind more resources on multiplayer. The achievements also suffer from these tedious tasks.

Aside from grinding things, the story was fine and they did a good job with it. Sure there may had been some stops here and there in the last Act that you have to go and fetch some things then come back several times which doesn't make sense, but other than that, it's enjoyable.

Another thing I want to mention is the performance. This, and the Oblivion Remaster, had been using all of my computer's resources, so 95% of the time, my memory was full and the CPU was working hard. If I had things running in the background, then the game would get stuttery.

After getting attacked twice today while gathering spice and almost losing my assault copther, I finally got enough spice to fully upgrade everything, and I'm finally done with the game. Just finished the final quest.
During the 180 hours of play time I crafted all MK6 equipment, all vehicles, built a nice base for my guild and unlocked all skills I found useful.
First 100 hours were amazing, I couldn't stop playing. And then I had to go to the Deep Desert. Last 80 hours felt more like work and only my completionism pushed me to play. Getting all that spice and plastanium was one the worst survival game experiences I had. Most of DD content is either repetitive or painful for someone not interested in PvP.
Unfortunately, most of my friends dropped the game long before we got a crawler, so I probably won't ever get to use it. So upsetting.
I loved this game and I hate it now. I got my money worth, but I'm dissatisfied.
Enjoy the game while it lasts, good luck everyone.

Really enjoying the game so far. The survival mechanics feel solid, and exploring Arrakis is a really immersive experience. Definitely living up to my expectations and looking forward to many hours in this game.

This game is well worth the money. The devs have listened to the community and made changes to appease the masses. In Sept. they are launching to consoles and bringing a massive update that will allow those who wish to play in single player mode the ability to do so. I am just amazed that the dev team cared enough to make the community happy.

For the first 100 hours, this game is fantastic. The story, gameplay, exploration, skill trees, character building, base building, and crafting; all wrapped in the incredible Dune universe, make for a deeply engaging experience.

But then you hit the endgame. At first, harvesting spice while dodging sandworms is thrilling. Soon, though, it becomes clear that everything you’ve worked for, skills, gear, faction choice, even your character build; is meaningless. In practice, you could just strip down, hop in an ornithopter, and play the same way.

On top of that, griefers ruin the experience. Groups with rocket launchers will hunt you down. You can’t outrun them, you can’t fight back (because you either have rockets or storage space and if you're farming you'll go with storage space), and when they destroy your hard-earned vehicle you lose everything you brought with you. They barely gain anything, but you’ve just wasted hours building your ornithopter, farming spice and flying across endless, empty dunes.

The result is a game that starts brilliantly but ends by wasting your time and making your progress feel pointless. Despite the great first 100 hours, I can’t recommend it.

Looking for a game that feels more like a second job?

Thrilled by the idea of losing everything just because you didn’t log in for a month to grind resources for your power generator?

Craving a "harsh, oppressive, unforgiving, deadly" world where water is supposedly more precious than life, yet the landscape is cluttered with player-made shacks overflowing with water and ornithopters?

Then Dune Awakening is for you. Just wait for a discount. This grindy, lore-starved mess is worth maybe 15€ on a good day, I was wrong to pay full price.

Don’t expect Herbert’s depth, just a lazy checklist: Spice! Desert! Worms!

The Atreides and Harkonnen are so neutered they might as well be random MMO factions. Everything else is generic filler content buried under endless grind and a sand-colored paper-thin veneer. It doesn't get better the more you play, quite the opposite, after 110h it's tedious and feels like a chore.

Frank Herbert is probably rolling in his grave by how his world was trashed and milked like this.

the game has evolved alot since release. great beginning since everything tries to kill you but once you unlock everything- there is very little danger to player. landsraad missions are also a FOMO inducing for endgame because if you care about progression, then you will need to repeat the same few missions until youre sick of them. if you miss your daily landsraad missions, you will lose them since at the moment you get 5 per day and they stack until cap of 35 and doing all missions in succession is mind numbing and boring. i have everything unlocked and i dont see the reason to return until new content releases.
This game is everything I would want as an immersive/interactive experience that's based on the recent Dune movies.

This game has been, and continues to be, ridiculously fun despite late game content being a bit repetitive in the very late game. Things like the rush for Lansraad and widespread communication between guilds for voting power or our guilds bi-weekly community event, Stioneheart Nights Racing, have been some of the most fun to I've had in a game in a very long time. 

The early game is very immersive, fun, and dangerous. It's some of the best content in the game and well worth taking your time to experience fully. The middle of the game you get a broader view of the world and it offers a lot of variability in how and where you play.. The late game can be very grindy but if you're into games that have a fairly consistent grind loop, it can be both painful and enjoyable. Painfully repetitive for specializations XP progress but enjoyable with friends new and old. 

8.5/10 *Absolutely worth it*

I love survival games, this one however just does not seem to keep my interest. I keep wondering what is next; the constant farming is not very rewarding, as it seems I have to spend more time traveling to a specific area to get a specific item that i may need every now and then. To be fair I am not at the end-game, but I am extremely close, and the fact that you have to farm so many materials to get your base up as well as keep a base up and running is simply not worth while to me. That as well as the fact that the end game is very boring and the PvP does not exist from what i can see, This PvE game is very lacking at a certain point and makes the routine of resource gathering not worth it in the long run,

I really wanted to like this game and I did for parts of it.
I played about 300 hours and I came to the conclusion that this is not a game for solo players.
The grind is just too difficult and the game is just not balanced in this regard.
The last straw came when I lost everything I've been working on for 2 weeks in a storm. My mistake or not, it's just not a good time in general when a game is that unforgiving .

I have to admit this game had me rage quit several times until I got use to the mechanics. However once I got familiar with the mechanics the change was like night and day, I fell in love with the game.
I lot of the UI is very much like Conan exiles but what was throwing me off was that I was expecting to do the same thing as Conan exiles but it's a completely different animal.

One of the things I really love about the game is how the survival mechanic is on a different level to other survival games. It's more the core than a routine. What really makes the game shine is the 100% atmosphere the game generates.
Also get's better with every update.
A game that belongs in your library.

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (72%): players mainly praise the story and characters.
Its main complaint is the content and grind, which many say is bland and repetitive.
